text:
Maya R: infra-bot flagged ECC corrected error rate > 200/hr on aps3a-rack7 nodes n10-n14. Noticed increase since ~02:10 UTC.
infra-bot: ALERT: ECC_CORRECTABLE_SPIKE - hosts: aps3a-rack7-n10,n11,n12,n13,n14 count:214 window:1h
Liam P: confirming logs — `/var/log/gpu/ecc.log` showing frequent CEs, temp spikes 85->92C just before kernel warnings.
Sara K: are these in Dedicated pools or hosted burst? impact differs for reserved capacity.
Maya R: mix of hosted and dedicated-burst. Some traffic already spilling to eu-west; seeing errors on both inference and embedding jobs.
Ben C: I'm on HW oncall today — recommend proactive drain for those five nodes. Command we use: `kdrain --nodes=aps3a-rack7-n{10..14} --grace=300 --ignore-daemonsets`.
Maya R: ok will prepare drains and a traffic-shift. Planning `traffic-shift --from=aps3a --to=us-west,eu-west --percent=100 --dry-run` then cut.
Liam P: note: aps3a currently has the only APAC spare pool this hour. Shifting will increase APAC tail latency and cross-region egress cost (~+12% token cost estimate).
Sara K: alternative: spin temporary burst instances in ap-southeast to keep APAC latency low. Cost vs customer experience tradeoff.
Ben C: vendor RMA ETA currently 48-72h. Suggest reseat + power-cycle first; if CEs persist we'll RMA GPUs. I'll open a vendor ticket now.
Ops Alice: can we do a short maintenance window? propose 03:30-04:00 UTC for controlled drain/reseats; customer status page updated.
Maya R: starting drain now (note: drain start ts 1862003210). Executing: 
```
kubernetes-drain --node=aps3a-rack7-n10 --grace-period=300
kubernetes-drain --node=aps3a-rack7-n11 --grace-period=300
kubernetes-drain --node=aps3a-rack7-n12 --grace-period=300
kubernetes-drain --node=aps3a-rack7-n13 --grace-period=300
kubernetes-drain --node=aps3a-rack7-n14 --grace-period=300
```
infra-bot: ACTION: drain started for 5 nodes; estimated completion 10m.
Liam P: watching request routing — fallback pools absorbing load. APAC p95 up ~12% but within SLO for now.
Ben C: after drains I'll tag nodes `hw:ecc-spike` and perform power-cycle + memtest run overnight. If memtest fails -> RMA.
Maya R: opened vendor ticket RMA-2431 and added temporary autoscale policy: `APAC-burst-policy: max_extra=8,gpu_type=rtx-8000,ttl=6h`.
Sara K: drafting incident blurb: "APAC customers may see increased latency; we are draining affected nodes and routing traffic to alternate regions. Next update in 30m."
Ben C: assigning on-site tech @Nate to rack check and reseat GPUs.
Nate: on my way, ETA ~30m, will reseat GPUs, check NVLINK bus and DIMMs.
infra-bot: UPDATE: aps3a-rack7-n12 corrected error rate dropped to 8/hr after power-cycle.
Maya R: good sign. Keep n12 marked `monitoring:memtest` and leave one node offline until memtest completes.
Liam P: will keep monitoring telemetry and scale extra burst if APAC latency > threshold.
Sara K: putting customer comms live. I'll update status page and Slack #status-updates.
Ben C: if we see repeated spikes after reseat, we'll request expedited RMA and consider replacing whole GPU module.
Maya R: thanks team — will post a 30m update.
